title: Eventual periodicity assembled from a stabilisation invariant and a modulus (IMO 2026 Q6)
intent: Prove the eventual periodicity of any valid sequence by lifting the number-theoretic heart (goodness stabilisation) into a threshold, then feeding that threshold and a prefix-product modulus to a 'from stable' transformer lemma that manufactures the period; the 6-line glue does no arithmetic of its own.

parent.name: eventual_periodicity
parent.statement:
theorem eventual_periodicity (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : IsValidSeq a) :
    ∃ N T L : ℕ, 0 < T ∧ 0 < L ∧ ∀ n, N ≤ n → a (n + T) = a n + L

    ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → ∀ b, Good a n b ↔ Good a N b

children.name: eventual_periodicity_from_stable
children.statement:
theorem eventual_periodicity_from_stable (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : IsValidSeq a)
    {N M : ℕ} (hMpos : 0 < M)
    (hstab : ∀ n, N ≤ n → ∀ b, Good a n b ↔ Good a N b)
    (hM : ∀ i ≤ N, ∀ p, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ a i → p ∣ M) :
    ∃ N' T L : ℕ, 0 < T ∧ 0 < L ∧ M ∣ L ∧
      ∀ n, N' ≤ n → a (n + T) = a n + L
children.closed_by: pigeonhole Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to on residues mod M, then induction on d whose step closes by le_antisymm of two greedy-minimality bounds

    ∀ i ≤ N, ∀ p, Nat.Prime p → p ∣ a i → p ∣ prefixMod a N

applicability.goal_shape: ∃ N T L, 0 < T ∧ 0 < L ∧ ∀ n, N ≤ n → a (n + T) = a n + L for a sequence a : ℕ → ℕ defined by a recursion whose predicate Good a n b depends on n only through the prefix a 0, …, a n
applicability.use_when: the argument factors into (i) a stabilising/limiting invariant (here goodness stabilising past a threshold), (ii) a modulus that absorbs the finitely many primes the prefix cares about, and (iii) a 'from stable' lemma parameterised by that invariant; each part is then a self-contained lemma and the glue is pure assembly
applicability.avoid_when: the invariant does not actually stabilise (the hard content is inside the invariant); the transformer is not parameterised by the invariant and must be re-proved per instance; or there is no finite modulus that absorbs the prefix primes

consequences: The move splits one theorem into a stabilisation invariant, two modulus facts, and a 'from stable' transformer, leaving the glue with no arithmetic. Obligations it creates: the invariant must genuinely stabilise (good_stabilizes_core is the hard part); the modulus must absorb every prime the prefix cares about (prefixMod_absorbs); and the transformer must be parameterised by the invariant, not by a concrete instance. Failure modes: if the stabilisation threshold and the modulus entangle, the transformer and the invariant leak into each other; if the transformer needs a different invariant than the one proved, the glue must redo the wiring instead of just instantiating.
